entries.why: All facts found in IFC ESRS 35701. Spring monitoring narrowed to medium-risk springs as the ESRS says; last sentence reworded to the ESRS wording ('must be managed in a manner consistent with' the Performance Standards).

CAO 2018 says IFC required the Performance Standards for 'new investments', not 'all operations it financed'; three-day notice limited to incidents affecting the Performance Standards, as the report says. Other facts confirmed.
HRW 2019 confirms the banks contractually required compliance with IFC Performance Standards and EHS Guidelines, the contractually binding ESAP and its aims, and non-disclosure of agreed measures.

Confirmed in ADB PAM (paras 41, 47, EMP list) and AIIB document. EMP approval is by the project unit (PIU), and the disbursement condition names CEO, CFO, procurement and safeguards officers; wording fixed.

The only 'condition' is GDF Suez's own eligibility rule for its 2014 green bond (BankTrack confirms the wording). That is the company's own rule set by the issuer, not a term a lender or bondholder attached to money for Jirau; the brief excludes the company's own rules. BNDES loan terms not found.
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.

AidData 61320 confirms collateral, ICBC agent, EPC contract and 2023 guaranteed loan; 'no sovereign guarantee' is stated for the USD tranche, so narrowed. 'tied' removed: AidData says the loan financed an EPC contract with Indonesian and Chinese firms but does not say the loan required Chinese contractors.
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.

The paper does say MCC 'has required' MCA-Lesotho to comply with OP 4.12, and MCC is a listed co-financier, so kept but credited to MCC's compact (not the World Bank) and to the implementer's own staff paper. Co-author name corrected (Lira Molapo, not 'Mahlao'). Dropped 'cash compensation paid before construction' (an outcome, not a term).

District court opinion confirms the IFC terms. ADB sentence dropped: the remedial action plan the borrower agreed on 19 June 2015 came seven years after the 2008 loan, after a compliance review, so it is not a term of the money at the time it was lent.

All items found in IFC ESRS 34203, but the land-take, biodiversity and third-party review items sit in an action plan updated in 2020-2021 (after amendments), not the 2015/2016 original; wording now says so. Source year corrected to 2015 (ESRS disclosure date).
No conditions proposed by researcher; nothing to check.

EIB Complaints Mechanism report quotes Finance Contract §1.04A(h) (RAP as first-tranche disbursement condition, under World Bank framework) and §6.05(e)(i) (environmental law incl. social effects). Confirmed. Text unchanged; 'why' quote replaced with a contiguous phrase (the old one used an ellipsis).

The proposed 2016-2019 World Bank loan was never approved (India withdrew the request in July 2019), so no money was lent then and nothing could be a condition of it. The text describes appraisal procedure and Bank-wide resettlement policy, not loan terms. No terms found for the 2024 loan.

RPF para 88 states this for this project's loan-financed sections, and the wording credits the planning document. Dropped the 'no relocation before compensation' line (an implementation instruction to the project unit) and the replacement-cost line (Management describing what the borrower's resettlement plan required, not a lender term).

The 2015 concept-stage safeguards sheet only said a resettlement plan 'may' be needed, so it is not a loan term; dropped it and the PAD 'supports implementation' line. Replaced with the Panel 2024 report (paras 375 and annex), where Management cites the Project Loan Agreement directly.

PAD confirms indemnity, put-option backstop and effectiveness conditions; the payment guarantee backs ENEO's PPA payments (not the government's), fixed. Dropped the SCAP sentence: per the 2022 Panel report NHPC committed to it later during supervision, so it is not a term of the money when lent.

Both reports confirm the quotes. Dropped 'the resettlement plans required compensation before works' as the lead: that is the borrower's plan, not a lender term. Kept the Bank's own no-objection requirement as stated by Management. No financing agreement seen.

PAD lists the escrow deposit as an effectiveness condition under the Financing Agreement and the account as a covenant; confirmed. Dropped 'land taken only after compensation' (PAD describing Bank-wide OP 4.12, not a project term) and the 15% revenue target (a results indicator, not a condition).
Panel 2022 report cites the Financing Agreement (Schedule 2) directly; confirmed. Added the resettlement plans the PAD also assigns to the contractor and UNRA's role.

ESIA summary confirms the wording; kept credited to the borrower's own planning document, which does not use 'required'. Dropped the April 2020 R$124 million cap: it is a restructuring term set four years after the 2016 loan, not a term of the money when lent.

PID/ISDS confirms both points for this project. Dropped 'disclosed before appraisal' (Bank-wide disclosure policy) and the 20% land security allowance (a provision of the borrower's 2018 resettlement plan, reported as an allegation in the Request, not a lender term).
